parole.testo: Borrowed from Manx ayr. Doublet of faeder, father, padre, pater, and père.
From Manx bollan bane (“white wort”), from bollan (“herb, wort”) + bane (“white”); compare Scottish Gaelic bàn.

parole.significato: A flat cake, sometimes made with dried fruit.
parole.testo: From Manx bonnag. Compare Irish bonnóg (“bannock, scone”), based on Latin pānicum (“millet”). Doublet of bannock.

parole.significato: A steep bank or grassy cliff.
The ragwort, the national flower of the Isle of Man, which has a large stalk.
parole.testo: From Manx cushag vooar (“big stalk”), from cushag (“stalk”).
From Manx jeeyl, jeeill ("damage"), cognate to Irish díobháil.

parole.significato: A traditional herbal beer from the Isle of Man.
A small monastic cell or chapel (especially during the pre-modern period).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Manx keeill. Doublet of cell.
